# Grammar Syntax

This chapter collects the syntax of a grammar file in one place. The grammar
below is written in PEGO itself and summarizes token structure and expression
forms. The chapters that define each construct remain normative for validation
and meaning.

The repository holds a full grammar of the language, `pego.pego`, which is the input
of the generated parser of grammar files. Its actions produce a typed source tree
with comments, source forms, and recoverable error nodes. This tree is separate from
the public `grammar.Grammar` AST.

The grammar is checked by tests, which run both views on every
`.pego` file of the repository and on every `pego` code block of the
documentation and require them to agree with the parser of the reference
implementation on whether the text is a valid grammar.

## Simple Grammar

This syntax view omits result types, Value Actions, captures, metadata attributes
and recovery handling. Unnecessary grouping is removed while retaining
parentheses required by precedence or source layout. Predicate Actions and matching pragmas remain, including
the state that controls physical newlines. Generate the view with
`pego fmt -syntax pego.pego` or `grammar.FormatSyntax(g)` in Go. This is a
readable projection: in other grammars, a predicate may depend on captures,
constructed values or types that the simplified view omits.

```pego
// PEGO grammar syntax and typed source tree.
// Source forms are preserved before semantic validation and compilation.
package pego

// File and statements. Delimiter-owned expressions enable multiline trivia;
// declaration and item lists keep physical newlines as statement boundaries.
rule main = file
rule file = &source_comments file_contents
rule file_contents = (
    {ml := false}
    package_entry?
    (-empty_stmts def_stmt)*
    -empty_stmts comments $$
)
rule empty_stmts = (";" -comments)*
rule package_entry = &(comments "package" !ident_char) package_stmt
rule package_stmt = (
    &source_remaining comments
    package_body &source_package_tail stmt_end
)
rule package_body = "package" -word_end #cut ident
rule source_package_tail = -";"? source_after_boundary
rule def_stmt = (
    !(comments $$)
    (type_def_stmt / rule_def_stmt / _|_)
)
rule stmt_end = horizontal stmt_sep
rule item_end = horizontal item_sep
rule field_end = horizontal field_sep
rule stmt_sep = block_sep / empty_stmt_sep
rule item_sep = block_sep / empty_item_sep
rule field_sep = block_sep / empty_field_sep
rule block_sep = block_with_line
rule empty_stmt_sep = ";" / nl / &$$
rule empty_item_sep = ";" / nl / &"}"
rule empty_field_sep = ";" / nl / &"}"
// Recovery consumes its own separator and stops before the next item.
rule stmt_sync = -comments (sync_token / !(";" / nl) .)* (";" / nl / &$$)
rule item_sync = -comments (sync_token / !(";" / nl / "}") .)* (";" / nl / &"}" / &$$)
rule field_sync = -comments (sync_token / !(";" / nl / "}") .)* (";" / nl / &"}" / &$$)

// Completed literals, nested comments and groups do not end recovery.
rule sync_token = string / char_class / inline_comment / comment_line / sync_paren / sync_brace
rule sync_paren = "(" (sync_token / !("(" / ")" / nl) .)* ")"
rule sync_brace = "{" (sync_token / !("{" / "}" / nl) .)* "}"

// Types. Union is the weakest operation; list and optional prefixes nest.
rule type_def_stmt = comments type_def_body stmt_end
// The body starts at the keyword and ends before the statement separator.
// Its typed node retains the actual parse span without repeating recovery.
rule type_def_body = (
    "type" -word_end #cut ident -ws
    type_spec
)
rule type_spec = struct_spec / terminal_spec / type_alias_spec
rule struct_spec = (
    "=" -ws "{" #cut {ml := false} field_spec* comments
    -"}"
)
rule field_spec = !(comments "}") field
rule field = (
    comments ident -ws
    type_expr field_end
)
rule terminal_spec = "terminal" !ident_char
rule type_alias_spec = "~" -ws type_expr
rule type_expr = operators {
    skip ws
    operand bottom
    operand ident type_args
    operand ident
    operand type_group
    operand struct_type
    level union { infix left "|" }
    level meet { infix left "&" }
    level prefix {
        prefix "[]"
        prefix "*"
    }
}

// An unnamed struct type has the fields of a struct definition.
rule struct_type = (
    "{" {ml := false} field_spec* comments
    -"}"
)

// The brackets of type arguments follow the name directly.
rule type_args = "[" {ml := true} -ws type_expr (-ws "," -ws type_expr)* -ws ","? -ws "]"

// A rule of its own keeps ml from reaching the rest of the type. Parentheses
// around one type without a comma group it; any other parentheses form a tuple.
rule type_group = type_paren / type_tuple
rule type_paren = "(" {ml := true} -ws type_expr -ws ")"
rule type_tuple = "(" {ml := true} -ws (type_expr -ws "," -ws)* type_expr? -ws ")"

// Rule expressions. The empty infix operator represents adjacency, so
// juxtaposition does not need a separate sequence parser or require a space.
rule rule_def_stmt = (
    comments "rule" -word_end #cut ident -ws type_expr? -ws
    -"=" -ws (ops_rule_expr / rule_expr) -ws whole_action? stmt_end
)
rule whole_action = "=>" -ws action
rule rule_expr = operators {
    skip ws
    operand rule_group / predicate / level_call / bottom / top / begin_input / begin_line / end_input / end_line / any / cut / string / char_class / rule_ref
    level ordered_choice { infix left "/" }
    level sequence { infix left _ }
    level prefix {
        prefix ident ":"
        prefix "&" / "!"
        prefix "-" !("-" / ">")
    }
    level suffix {
        postfix "?"
        postfix "*"
        postfix "+"
        postfix "#atomic" !ident_char (empty_args / !"(")
        postfix "#stream" !ident_char (empty_args / !"(")
        postfix "#missing" !ident_char !"("
        postfix "#repeat" !ident_char repeat_args
        postfix "#recover" !ident_char recover_args
        postfix attr
    }
}
rule rule_group = (
    "(" {ml := true} -ws (inline_action / rule_expr) -ws
    -")"
)
rule inline_action = rule_expr -ws "=>" -ws action
rule rule_ref = ident !"("
rule level_call = (
    "level(" {ml := true} -ws #cut ident -ws
    -"," -ws
    ident -ws
    -")"
)
rule top = "_" !ident_char
rule bottom = "_|_"
rule begin_input = "^^"
rule begin_line = "^"
rule end_input = "$$"
rule end_line = "$" !(ident_start / digit)
rule any = "."
rule cut = "#cut" !ident_char !"("
rule predicate = action_block
rule repeat_args = (
    "(" {ml := true} -ws (repeat_range / repeat_count) -ws
    -")"
)
rule repeat_range = repeat_from / repeat_to
rule repeat_from = repeat_int -ws "," -ws repeat_int?
rule repeat_to = "," -ws repeat_int
rule repeat_count = repeat_int
rule repeat_int = (digit+ / "-" -ws "0"+ !digit) #atomic
rule recover_args = (
    "(" {ml := true} -ws -"skip" -word_end
    -"=" -ws rule_expr -ws
    -")"
)
rule empty_args = "(" {ml := true} -ws ")"
rule attr = "@" ident (attr_args / attr_no_args)
rule attr_args = (
    "(" {ml := true} -ws (attr_no_values / attr_named_args / attr_mixed_args) -ws
    -")"
)
rule attr_named_args = attr_named (-ws "," -ws attr_named)* (-ws "," -ws)?
rule attr_mixed_args = attr_slot (-ws "," -ws attr_slot)* (attr_named_tail / attr_empty_args)
rule attr_no_args = !"("
rule attr_no_values = &")"
rule attr_empty_args = _
rule attr_named_tail = -ws "," -ws attr_named_args
rule attr_slot = !(ident -ws "=") attr_value?
rule attr_named = ident -ws "=" -ws attr_value
rule attr_value = true / false / nil / signed_int / string / rule_expr
rule signed_int = ("-" -ws)? digit+ #atomic

// Operators Rule items and each level recover independently. An absent level
// name remains nil; level(rule, name) can target only named levels.
rule ops_rule_expr = (
    "operators" !ident_char -ws &"{" #cut "{" {ml := false} (-empty_stmts ops_stmt)* -empty_stmts
    comments -"}"
)
rule ops_stmt = (
    !(comments "}")
    (ops_skip_stmt / ops_operand_stmt / ops_level_stmt / _|_)
)
rule ops_skip_stmt = comments "skip" -word_end #cut rule_expr item_end
rule ops_operand_stmt = (
    comments "operand" -word_end #cut rule_expr -ws
    whole_action? item_end
)
rule ops_level_stmt = (
    comments "level" -word_end #cut ident? -ws
    -"{" (-empty_stmts ops_operator)*
    -empty_stmts comments -"}" item_end
)
rule ops_operator = (
    !(comments "}")
    (ops_prefix / ops_postfix / ops_infix / _|_)
)
rule ops_prefix = (
    comments "prefix" -word_end #cut rule_expr -ws
    whole_action? item_end
)
rule ops_postfix = (
    comments "postfix" -word_end #cut rule_expr -ws
    whole_action? item_end
)
rule ops_infix = (
    comments "infix" -word_end #cut
    ("left" / "right" / "none")
    -word_end rule_expr -ws whole_action? item_end
)

// Predicate Actions and Value Actions share statement syntax. The source AST
// retains unsupported blocks and inline actions for later compilation checks.
rule action = default_action / action_block / action_expr
rule default_action = "..."
rule action_block = (
    "{" {ml := false} action_block_stmt* comments
    -"}"
)
rule action_block_stmt = !(comments "}") action_block_value
rule action_block_value = -comments action_stmt -item_end
rule action_stmt = action_assign_stmt / action_expr
rule action_assign_stmt = ident -ws ":=" -ws action_expr
rule action_expr = lambda / action_ops
rule action_ops = operators {
    skip ws
    operand list_constructor / terminal_constructor / constructor / call / action_group / int / string / true / false / nil / capture_ref / var_ref
    level disjunction { infix left "||" }
    level conjunction { infix left "&&" }
    level comparison { infix none "==" / "!=" / "<=" / ">=" / "<" / ">" }
    level addition { infix left "+" / "-" !("-" / ">") }
    level multiplication { infix left "*" / "/" / "%" }
    level unary { prefix "-" !"-" / "!" !"=" }
    // x[i] indexes a list. The reference parser takes "[" as an index only directly after a name,
    // a capture, ")" or "]", and reads it as a character class elsewhere. This grammar is looser
    // both ways: skip ws accepts "x [i]", and a rule body accepts "name[a-z]" as a reference
    // followed by a character class, which the reference parser rejects.
    level field_access {
        postfix "." -ws capture_ref
        postfix "." -ws cast_type
        postfix "." -ws ident
        postfix "[" -ws action_expr -ws "]"
    }
}
// A rule of its own keeps ml from reaching the rest of the action.
rule cast_type = "(" {ml := true} -ws type_expr -ws ")"
rule lambda = "(" {ml := true} -ws lambda_params? -ws ")" -ws "=>" -ws action_expr
rule lambda_params = ident (-ws "," -ws ident)*
rule action_group = (
    "(" {ml := true} -ws action_expr -ws
    -")"
)
rule call = (
    var_name "(" {ml := true} -ws #cut action_args? -ws
    -")"
)
rule action_args = action_expr (-ws "," -ws action_expr)* (-ws "," -ws)?
rule list_constructor = (
    "[]" -ws #cut level(type_expr, prefix) -ws
    -"{" {ml := true} -ws
    action_args? comments -"}"
)
rule terminal_constructor = (
    var_name -ws "{" {ml := true} -ws !("}" / ident -ws ":") #cut
    action_args comments -"}"
)
rule constructor = (
    var_name -ws "{" {ml := true} -ws #cut constructor_fields? comments
    -"}"
)
rule constructor_fields = init_field (-ws "," -ws init_field)* (-ws "," -ws)?
rule init_field = (
    comments ident -ws -":" -ws
    action_expr
)
rule int = digit+ #atomic
rule true = "true" !ident_char
rule false = "false" !ident_char
rule nil = "nil" !ident_char
rule capture_ref = "$" ident #atomic
rule var_name = ident
rule var_ref = ident !"("

// Trivia. Space is discarded before and after each retained comment, keeping
// the resulting list homogeneous without introducing nil whitespace elements.
rule ws = {ml} comments / horizontal
rule comments = -space* (comment -space*)*
rule horizontal = -space_no_line* ((line_comment / block_no_line) -space_no_line*)*
rule word_end = !ident_char -ws
rule space_no_line = !nl space
rule nl = "\r\n" / [\r\n]
rule space = [ \t\n\u{b}\u{c}\r\u{85}\u{a0}\u{1680}\u{2000}-\u{200a}\u{2028}\u{2029}\u{202f}\u{205f}\u{3000}]
// A lexical comment view retains trivia inside parsing and action expressions.
// Incomplete tokens remain available to the error-recovering structural pass.
rule source_comments = -source_non_comment* (comment -source_non_comment*)* $$
rule source_non_comment = source_string / source_class / incomplete_comment / !("//" / "/*") .
rule source_string = "\"" ("\\" . / [^"\\\n])* "\""?
rule source_class = "[" ("\\" . / [^\]\\\n])* "]"?
rule incomplete_comment = !inline_comment "/*" .* $$
rule comment = comment_group / inline_comment
rule comment_group = comment_line (-nl -space_no_line* comment_line)*
rule line_comment = comment_line
rule comment_line = ("//" [^\n\r]*) #atomic
rule inline_comment = "/*" (inline_comment / !("/*" / "*/") .)* #atomic "*/"
rule block_no_line = "/*" (block_no_line / !("/*" / "*/" / nl) .)* #atomic "*/"
rule block_with_line = (
    "/*"
    ((block_no_line / !("/*" / "*/" / nl) .)* (nl / block_with_line) (inline_comment / !("/*" / "*/") .)*)
    #atomic "*/"
)
rule ident = (ident_start ident_char*) #atomic
rule ident_start = [a-zA-Z_]
rule ident_char = [a-zA-Z0-9_]
rule digit = [0-9]
rule string = "\"" ("\\" escape_char / [^"\\\n])* "\"" #atomic
rule char_class = (
    "[" "^"? (char_class_rng / char_class_chr)+
    -"]"
)
rule char_class_rng = char_class_chr "-" !"]" char_class_chr
rule char_class_chr = ("\\" escape_char / [^\]\\\n]) #atomic
rule escape_char = "u{" [0-9a-fA-F]+ "}" / "u" [0-9a-fA-F] #repeat(4) / [ntrfvab0] / [^a-zA-Z0-9]

// Normalized declaration ownership, independent of raw formatter comments.
rule source_after_boundary = (
    source_inline_line_boundary / source_inline_block_boundary / source_ambiguous_block_boundary
    / source_newline_boundary / source_remaining
)
rule source_inline_line_boundary = -source_horizontal source_line_comment source_remaining
rule source_inline_block_boundary = (
    -source_horizontal source_block_comment &(source_horizontal (source_nl / source_comment_start / $$))
    source_remaining
)
// One inline block ending on the next token's line is ambiguous, not trailing.
rule source_ambiguous_block_boundary = -source_horizontal source_block_comment -source_horizontal &source_next_token
rule source_newline_boundary = -source_horizontal -source_nl -source_horizontal (source_first_trailing / source_empty_comment) source_remaining

// A first standalone group can trail the previous declaration when a blank
// line, another group, or the end of a scope flushes it before the next token.
rule source_first_trailing = source_line_group &source_line_flush / source_block_comment &source_block_flush
rule source_remaining = source_scope_tail / source_next_boundary
rule source_scope_tail = -source_space* (source_comment -source_space*)* &source_scope_end
rule source_next_boundary = -source_space* (source_detached_group -source_space*)* (source_leading_group / source_empty_comment) -source_space* &source_next_token
rule source_empty_comment = _
rule source_detached_group = source_line_group &source_line_flush / source_block_comment &source_block_flush
rule source_leading_group = source_comment -source_space* &source_next_token
rule source_line_flush = source_horizontal (source_nl / "/*" / source_scope_end)
rule source_block_flush = source_horizontal (source_nl source_horizontal (source_nl / source_comment_start / source_scope_end) / source_comment_start / source_scope_end)
rule source_next_token = !(source_space / source_comment_start / source_scope_end) .
rule source_scope_end = ")" / "]" / "}" / $$
rule source_comment_start = "//" / "/*"
rule source_comment = source_line_group / source_block_comment
rule source_line_group = source_line_comment (-source_horizontal source_line_comment)*
rule source_line_comment = "//" [^\r\n]* source_nl?
rule source_block_comment = "/*" source_block_line (source_nl -source_horizontal -source_block_star? source_block_line)* "*/"
rule source_block_star = "*" !"/"
rule source_block_line = source_block_piece*
rule source_block_piece = source_nested_piece / source_character_piece
rule source_nested_piece = source_block_comment
rule source_character_piece = (!(source_nl / "*/" / "/*") .) #atomic
rule source_nl = "\r\n" / [\r\n]
rule source_horizontal = source_horizontal_char*
rule source_horizontal_char = [ \t\u{b}\u{c}\u{85}\u{a0}\u{1680}\u{2000}-\u{200a}\u{2028}\u{2029}\u{202f}\u{205f}\u{3000}]
rule source_space = source_horizontal_char / source_nl
```

## What the Grammar Does Not Express

The grammar includes the ASCII identifier form. Names beginning with `_` are
parsed and preserved, then rejected by semantic validation. The following
additional constraints are checked outside this source grammar.

- **Reserved identifiers.** Names beginning with `_` are reserved. The
  standalone Rule Expression `_` is Top, which is distinct from a name.
- **Integer literals.** An [integer literal](lexical.md#integer-literals)
  MUST be representable as an `int`.
- **Character class ranges.** In `lo-hi`, `hi` MUST NOT be less than `lo`, and a
  class MUST contain at least one item.
- **Repetition bounds.** In `a #repeat(n,m)`, `m` MUST NOT be less than `n`.
- **Statement boundaries.** Newlines and semicolons separate Definition Statements and
  Operators Rule items. Struct fields use semicolons or newlines. An expression may
  cross a newline only within its own open delimiter; statement-list braces do
  not enable continuation of every nested expression. Indentation is not syntax.
- **Attribute arguments.** Positional arguments follow the generic value
  forms and precede named arguments; repeated named keys are rejected. The
  grammar models argument shape and ordering, not key uniqueness.
- **Contextual words.** Definition Statement and Operators Rule item introducers
  have their syntactic meaning only at those statement positions. They remain identifiers elsewhere.
- **Where constructs may appear.** An Operators Rule MUST be a complete Rule Definition Statement; a lambda MUST be an argument of `foldl`, `foldr` or `map`; and
  `#stream` MUST be at the top level of a rule body. A comment in a Definition Statement
  or Operators Rule statement header is rejected by semantic analysis with a
  positioned diagnostic. These checks follow parsing.
- **Action blocks.** Multiple-statement Predicate Actions and every braced
  Value Action are retained in the source AST but compilation rejects them.
- **Inline actions.** `(expression => action)` is recognized in the source
  grammar and represented in the AST, but compilation rejects it. Runtime
  execution is not implemented.
- **Attribute placement.** Attributes are postfix Rule Expression annotations;
  Definition Statement prefixes are not supported.

## Operators

Rule Expressions bind in the order of the [precedence
table](parser-expressions.md#precedence). Action Expressions in Value Actions
and Predicate Actions bind in the order of the [operator
table](actions.md#operators-and-functions):
`||`, `&&`, comparison (`==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, which do not chain),
`+` and `-`, `*`, `/` and `%`, and the unary `-` and `!`. Field access (`.`),
capture access (`.$`), indexing (`[i]`) and function calls bind tighter than
the operators. A `[`
written directly after a name, a capture reference, `)` or `]` is an index
bracket; elsewhere it begins a character class. Each Operators Rule defines
precedence by the order of its `level` declarations; associativity and operator
order come from entries within each level. The Operators Rule represents
adjacency with an empty infix operator and gives postfix modifiers tighter
binding than capture,
lookahead and discard. Ordered choice remains the weakest operation.
